title: Orientation Propagation Artifact v0.1
description: A CPDAG plus external direction constraints, closed under Meek's rules R1-R4. A standalone artifact: it says its own `kind`. It echoes its INPUTS as well as its outputs — `input_directed`, `input_undirected`, `constraints`, and both kinds of asserted adjacency — because `verify_orientation_propagation` re-derives the closure from a second transcription of Meek's rules and must not have to ask the producer what it was given. Every conflict here is a thing NOT applied: an assertion that contradicts the data is recorded and the data's structure left intact for a human to adjudicate, which is why the conflict list is part of the answer rather than an error channel.

nodes.description: Every node in the graph, sorted.

input_directed.description: The orientations the DATA established — the unshielded colliders. Each pair reads tail-then-head. A constraint that contradicts one of these is refused, not applied.

input_undirected.description: The undetermined edges as given, each sorted so the same pair always writes the same way.

constraints.description: Required directions, tail-then-head, in the order they were applied. Order is part of the record: a constraint may conflict with an EARLIER one, so which of two contradicting constraints was applied is a fact about this sequence.

oriented.description: Every directed edge after the closure — the data's colliders, the applied constraints, and everything R1-R4 forced from them.

remaining_undirected.description: What is still undetermined. Empty means the equivalence class collapsed to one DAG.

asserted_adjacencies.description: Pairs external knowledge claims are directly connected. Checked against the data's independence structure; never applied to the skeleton either way, because editing the skeleton would invalidate the collider structure that was read off it.

asserted_absences.description: The mirror: pairs external knowledge claims are independent — edges to drop. Same treatment, and for the same reason.

conflicts.description: Everything the caller asked for that was NOT done, and why. Three keys name which kind of input raised it — `constraint`, `assertion`, `absence` — and exactly one of the three is present per entry.

provenance.description: One entry per edge in `oriented`, saying what forced it. This is what makes the taint in `orientation_ledger_export` derivable: an edge forced by R2 from an LLM-proposed root is itself LLM-proposed, and only this record can say so.

conflictReason.description: Why the input was refused. `undermines_collider` is the interesting one: the assertion is not merely inconsistent with an edge, it would destroy the v-structure the data's orientations were read off — so the apexes at risk travel with it.

constraint.description: The refused direction, tail-then-head, exactly as the caller gave it.

data_edge.description: For `contradicts_data_orientation`: the orientation the data established, which is what the constraint ran into.

colliders.description: For `undermines_collider`: the apex nodes whose v-structure the assertion would destroy.

rule.description: What forced this orientation: the data (`collider_input`), an applied constraint, or one of Meek's four rules. R4 is what makes the closure complete once a constraint has been applied — R1-R3 alone are complete only for a CPDAG straight out of the data.

roots.description: The applied constraints this orientation ultimately rests on, tail-then-head. Empty for a data collider, which rests on nothing external. This is the transitive answer, not the immediate witness: an edge forced by R2 from an edge forced by R1 from a constraint carries that constraint here.
